chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who says, 'He is a Jew or a Christian, if he does not do such and such,' and he said, 'It is of no consequence.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: It is of no consequence / It is nothing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a conditional oath where the condition is not fulfilled?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on conditional oaths (*al-yamin al-mu'allaqah*) where the condition involves a specific action or state. The Imam clarifies that if a person swears conditionally (e.g., 'If I do X, I am a Jew'), and the condition is not met or the action is not performed, the oath is considered 'of no consequence' (*laysa bi-shay'*), meaning it does not take effect as a binding oath requiring expiation. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that such oaths do not automatically trigger *kaffarah* (expiation) unless the specific condition is fulfilled, distinguishing them from absolute oaths.
